questions.q: The proportionate (partial goodwill) method of measuring non-controlling interest results in:
o: Goodwill recognised only for the parent's share
No difference vs full goodwill method
NCI measured at fair value of its shares
questions.why: Under the partial-goodwill (proportionate share of net assets) method, goodwill includes only the parent's share; NCI at its proportionate share of identifiable net assets. The alternative measures NCI at fair value (full goodwill).
questions.trend: Core concept that appears in some avatar in most attempts under the new scheme (pattern estimate).
questions.probWhy: HIGH likelihood for Nov 2026 — goodwill method comparison appears in almost every consolidation MCQ set Prediction is study guidance, not an ICAI statement.

mem.tip: Two goodwill doors: partial = parent only; full = everyone's, NCI gets fair value. Same assets, different doors — pick per question, never mix.
mem.link: Ch 13

questions.q: Parent sells inventory to a 80%-owned subsidiary at a profit of Rs 20 crore (upstream). At the reporting date the inventory remains unsold outside the group. The unrealised-profit elimination hits:
o: Consolidated inventory and the SELLER's profit — hence NCI gets 20% of the elimination in upstream sales
Consolidated inventory only, with no NCI effect
Subsidiary's revenue and only 80% of its profit
questions.why: Upstream (sub sells to parent): unrealised profit is eliminated against the seller's (sub's) profits, so NCI bears its share. Downstream: parent absorbs it fully. The elimination also reduces inventory to group cost.
questions.trend: Known trap zone: ICAI objective papers repeatedly test limits/exceptions of this rule (pattern estimate).
questions.probWhy: Realistic likelihood for Nov 2026 — direction-of-sale determines NCI effect — an evergreen trap AI prediction, not a certainty.

mem.tip: Upstream = sub's profit is dirty; NCI shares the scrub. Downstream = parent alone scrubs. Follow the goods; the elimination chases the seller.
mem.link: Ch 13

questions.q: A parent acquires a subsidiary on 1 October. The consolidated statement of profit or loss for that year includes the subsidiary's results:
o: For the full year, adjusting for the shortfall
From 1 October (acquisition date) to year-end only
From the start of the next financial year
questions.why: Ind AS 110 includes the subsidiary's post-acquisition income and expenses in consolidated P&L; comparatives are not restated (unlike the old pooling-style methods).
questions.trend: Core concept that appears in some avatar in most attempts under the new scheme (pattern estimate).
questions.probWhy: Realistic likelihood for Nov 2026 — inclusion-date mechanics reappear as standalone MCQs AI prediction, not a certainty.

mem.tip: Control from 1 Oct ⇒ consolidate from 1 Oct. The acquirer buys future cash flows, not past P&L.
mem.link: Ch 13

questions.q: An investment entity must measure subsidiaries at:
o: Fair value through profit or loss instead of consolidating
questions.why: Ind AS 110 exception: investment entities measure/control-fund subsidiaries at FVTPL rather than consolidating — unless a subsidiary provides investment services supporting the parent's investing activities (then consolidate).
questions.trend: No dominant past-pattern signal; included for balanced coverage (AI judgement).
questions.probWhy: Lower likelihood but possible — rare but decisive 'skip consolidation' case Included so a low-probability surprise cannot catch you cold.

mem.tip: Investment entities skip consolidation for pure investment subs — but keep them if the sub serves the investing business itself.

questions.q: Significant influence is generally presumed at voting power of:
questions.why: Ind AS 28 presumes significant influence at 20% or more of voting power (directly or through subsidiaries) unless clearly demonstrated otherwise; proof in the pudding also includes board representation, policy participation, material transactions.
questions.trend: Core concept that appears in some avatar in most attempts under the new scheme (pattern estimate).
questions.probWhy: Realistic likelihood for Nov 2026 — the 20% presumption is a standard quickie AI prediction, not a certainty.

mem.tip: 20% = presumption seatbelt for associates; 50%+ crosses into control. Between? Evidence decides.
mem.link: Ch 13

questions.q: In separate financial statements, investments in subsidiaries may be carried at:
o: Fair value or equity method only
Cost, Ind AS 109 (FVOCI/FVTPL), or Ind AS 28 equity method
Revaluation model of Ind AS 16 only
questions.why: Ind AS 27: in separate FS, account at cost, under Ind AS 109, or using the equity method (policy by class).
questions.trend: No dominant past-pattern signal; included for balanced coverage (AI judgement).
questions.probWhy: Lower likelihood but possible — the three-choice menu is a quickie Included so a low-probability surprise cannot catch you cold.

mem.tip: Separate FS give three menu items — cost, fair value (109), equity method. No consolidation here; that's a group luxury.

questions.q: An investor holds 45% of voting rights; the remaining 55% is widely dispersed with no collective arrangement, with 28% typically voting at AGMs and 17% against on all issues. Under Ind AS 110, power assessment focuses on:
o: Rights that give the CURRENT ability to direct relevant activities, including practical voting patterns
questions.why: Power = existing rights giving current ability to direct relevant activities; with dispersed holdings, practical voting patterns and other contractual arrangements matter — de facto control possible below 50%.
questions.trend: Core concept that appears in some avatar in most attempts under the new scheme (pattern estimate).
questions.probWhy: Realistic likelihood for Nov 2026 — de-facto-control scenarios are the new-scheme favourite AI prediction, not a certainty.

mem.tip: 45-plus-dispersed can still command: power is who can win today's votes, not the cap table's optics.
mem.link: Ch 13

questions.q: A joint operation (vs joint venture) gives the joint operator rights to:
o: The assets, and obligations for the liabilities, relating to the arrangement
Consolidated revenues of a separate vehicle
questions.why: Ind AS 111: joint operation ⇒ recognise its share of assets/liabilities/revenues/expenses; joint venture ⇒ equity method (net assets).
questions.trend: No dominant past-pattern signal; included for balanced coverage (AI judgement).
questions.probWhy: Lower likelihood but possible — rights-to-assets-vs-net-assets fork Included so a low-probability surprise cannot catch you cold.

mem.tip: Get your hands on the assets directly (operation) or claim a slice of the net (venture) — the vehicle's legal form + terms decide.

questions.q: Cobalt Ltd acquires 70% of a subsidiary for Rs 360 lakh when its net identifiable assets (at FV) are Rs 500 lakh. NCI is measured at its proportionate share of net assets. Consolidated goodwill is:
o: Rs 10 lakh (goodwill only for parent's share)
questions.why: NCI = 30% × 500 = Rs 150 lakh. Goodwill = 360 + 150 − 500 = Rs 10 lakh — the partial-goodwill result; NCI shares no goodwill.
questions.trend: Repeated theme in recent ICAI exam question-patterns for this paper (AI pattern estimate — not a citation to a specific past paper question).
questions.probWhy: HIGH likelihood for Nov 2026 — goodwill computation with the NCI method tag is asked in most consolidations Prediction is study guidance, not an ICAI statement.

mem.tip: Partial goodwill: goodwill = consideration + NCI-at-proportionate-net-assets − net assets acquired. Post-acquisition profits belong to group per %.
